daily.title: Live updates: Trump welcomes Xi to Washington
daily.summary: Donald Trump welcomes Xi Jinping to the US by greeting him personally at the tarmac at Joint Base Andrews. The two are expected to discuss trade, AI, Taiwan and Iran.

daily.title: Berlin Airport briefly suspends flights over drone sighting
daily.summary: Airspace over the German capital was closed for about 45 minutes after a drone was spotted on the runway. Flights have resumed but are experiencing delays.

daily.title: Harvey Weinstein resentenced to 15 years for sexual assault
daily.summary: The disgraced Hollywood mogul was found guilty of sexually assaulting former production assistant Miriam Haley. The man whose case spurred the #MeToo movement awaits a separate sentencing in a California rape case.

daily.title: New fighting in Ethiopia's Tigray region raises fears of a return to the country's civil war
daily.summary: Fighting in and around Tigray is testing Ethiopia's fragile 2022 peace deal. With old enemies forming new alliances, experts warn that the conflict could enter a dangerous new phase.

daily.title: Eviction of 87-year-old woman sparks housing protests in Madrid
daily.summary: Police escorted Maricarmen Abascal from the apartment she had called home for more than seven decades. The case has reignited debate over Spain's housing crisis, rising rents and protections for long-term tenants.

daily.title: Trump's Board of Peace proposes $2.45B for reconstruction in Gaza
daily.summary: The board has noted that the Palestinian enclave needs roughly $35.2 billion for full, medium-term reconstruction. Trump's plan for peace in Gaza has largely stalled since an agreement was reached almost a year ago.

daily.title: Who is skipping the UN General Assembly — and why
daily.summary: Xi Jinping, Vladimir Putin, Friedrich Merz, Giorgia Meloni and Mahmoud Abbas are among more than 50 leaders who won't make it to the UN General Assembly. Their reasons range from illness and domestic affairs to holidays.

daily.title: Could a Left Party government in Berlin expropriate large real estate companies?
daily.summary: The socialist Left Party won the Berlin election partly on the promise to implement the city's 2021 expropriation referendum as a way to solve the city's rent crisis. But can it really happen?

daily.title: China's 13-year-old swimming star raises questions on child athletes
daily.summary: Three gold medals and three Asian Games records have catapulted China's Yu Zidi, 13, into the sporting spotlight. She is far from the first teen prodigy, but should teens be competing at elite level?

daily.title: Pakistan's jailed former PM Khan's sons told DW the authorities are cracking down ahead of new PTI protests
daily.summary: The sons of jailed Pakistani ex-PM Imran Khan told DW their father is in ill health while being isolated from family and doctors. Other relatives have been detained ahead of a planned opposition protest.

daily.title: Slovakia: PM Robert Fico's NATO Article 5 remarks spark criticism and raise questions about his country's NATO commitment
daily.summary: Slovak Prime Minister Robert Fico says he fears war and will do everything he can to keep his country out of one. Critics say his remarks risk weakening NATO, the alliance that was designed to prevent such a war.

daily.title: Germany's oldest party, the center-left SPD, is in a difficult position following its success in the Mecklenburg-Western Pomerania state election
daily.summary: Chancellor Friedrich Merz (CDU) has vowed to press ahead with controversial reforms, but resistance is mounting within his coalition partner, the SPD. How much dissent can a governing coalition tolerate?

daily.title: Ethiopia: Fighting resumes in Tigray
daily.summary: Rebels in northern Ethiopia have seized regional airports and engaged government troops in Afar and Amhara. Observers fear deadly clashes could expand after rebels announced a new anti-government alliance.

daily.title: ICC convicts CAR ex-rebel leader of crimes against humanity
daily.summary: The International Criminal Court has found Mahamat Said Abdel Kani guilty of overseeing torture and other crimes. He headed a feared prison unit that held political prisoners.

daily.title: As the EU advances free trade with Southeast Asia, why is there no ASEAN-wide deal?
daily.summary: After years of arduous negotiations, the EU is closing on a string of bilateral trade deals with countries in Southeast Asia. And yet, a bloc-to-bloc agreement between the EU and ASEAN remains a distant prospect.

daily.title: Munich, Berlin, Cologne-Rhine-Ruhr – Germany's three Olympic candidates
daily.summary: Munich, Berlin, or the Cologne-Rhine-Ruhr region? Germany aims to host the Olympic Games again. Three candidates are in the running, with one city considered the slight favorite.

daily.title: Rome's Colosseum closes after worker falls to his death
daily.summary: The man had been working on a new lighting installation in the iconic Roman amphitheater. Italian authorities said they were working on determining the circumstances of the accident.

daily.title: Hungary: EU Commission wants to unblock €4.2b in funding
daily.summary: The Commission's president has argued that Budapest is strengthening the rule of law with Viktor Orban finally out of office. Funds had been blocked over corruption allegations under Hungary's former government.

daily.title: OECD says growth 'resilient' in 2026 despite Middle East war
daily.summary: The OECD group of industrialized nations put its 2026 growth forecast at 2.9%. It said investment in AI was helping drive growth, while the war in the Middle East was fueling inflation.

daily.title: Campus Project 2026: Georgia Takes Center Stage
daily.summary: The Beethovenfest exchange project brings German and Georgian musical traditions together. And the reasons go beyond music.

daily.title: El Nino explained: How the weather pattern affects hurricanes and tropical storms
daily.summary: From drought to major floods and extreme heat, El Nino will have a huge impact on the world's weather. In the Atlantic, it could mean a season without hurricanes.

daily.title: China's new travel rules unsettle tech giants and talent
daily.summary: Beijing is locking the gates to stop expertise and capital in strategic industries from fleeing. The country accused of industrial-scale intellectual property theft now fears the West will take its own.

daily.title: Famine threatens the Ukrainian town of Oleshky in the southern Kherson region as Russia delays creating a humanitarian evacuation corridor
daily.summary: Food supplies to the town of Oleshky in the occupied part of the southern Kherson region have been cut off since May. Efforts by Kyiv to negotiate the evacuation of civilians with Moscow have been largely unsuccessful.

daily.title: Germany news: Call to scrap once-a-day gas price rises
daily.summary: The ADAC motoring association says a once-a-day rule on gas price changes has failed to help drivers' wallets. Entry-level jobs are becoming scarcer, making things hard for those entering the job market. DW has more.

weekly.title: Military aircraft crashes near US air base in Spangdahlem, Germany
weekly.summary: The F-16 pilot was able to safely eject from the plane and was taken to receive medical care. The incident occurred near Spangdahlem Air Base in the German state of Rhineland-Palatinate.

weekly.title: Young Berliners vote overwhelmingly for socialist Left  Party
weekly.summary: Berlin's young voters overwhelmingly supported the victorious socialist Left Party. Are the young more radical? Or are the election results just a reflection of current German politics?

weekly.title: Living in the shadow of LA's hidden oil wells
weekly.summary: Many lifelong residents of Los Angeles have health impacts from growing up close to oil extraction. Now, the city is trying to close down the worst offenders, but it's an enormous task.

weekly.title: Could we see MMA at the Olympics?
weekly.summary: Mixed martial arts has made its debut at the Asian Games this week. It takes the sport closer to the Olympics but there are doubts about the next step, and the influence of the popular and lucrative UFC.

weekly.title: Male infertility is 'grossly underreported'
weekly.summary: It's not all on women anymore — doctors do test men for sperm count and motility. But still too few men get checked, possibly due to a misconception that a healthy sex life means healthy sperm. Spoiler: It doesn't.

weekly.title: 'Swan Song': New book by Princess Diana's brother drops
weekly.summary: A memoir penned by Charles Spencer on his older sister's life has been released, opening old royal wounds nearly three decades after Princess Diana's death.

weekly.title: Will Germany have enough gas this winter amid energy supply crunch?
weekly.summary: Germany's gas storage sites are far less full than in recent years. Officials say supplies are secure, but analysts warn that a cold winter or import disruptions could push prices higher. So how secure is the supply?

weekly.title: Germany news: VW to step up cost-cutting program
weekly.summary: Volkswagen's chief says the carmaker will accelerate its streamlining measures as workers protest. The Israeli ambassador says the Left Party win in Berlin polls poses a risk to the city's Jewish community. DW has more.

weekly.title: How will Germany's Merz respond after crushing state election results and losses to the far right?
weekly.summary: Germany's far-right AfD and the socialist Left Party gained ground in recent state elections, while the centrist parties lost support. The biggest loser is Chancellor Friedrich Merz.

weekly.title: Princess Diana's brother makes explosive claims about royals in new memoir
weekly.summary: Here are some of the key revelations from Charles Earl Spencer's highly anticipated memoir "Swan Song: Diana, My Sister." It has already provoked Buckingham Palace to react.

weekly.title: Germany news: Trial starts of ex-Transport Minister Scheuer
weekly.summary: Former Transport Minister Andreas Scheuer is being tried for perjury related to a failed car toll scheme. And cherry farmers have brought in a bumper harvest.

weekly.title: Germany's car crisis: Can the 35-hour workweek survive?
weekly.summary: German carmakers want employees to work 40 hours instead of the current 35 without extra pay, arguing it would improve competitiveness. Unions strongly oppose the proposal and view it as an attack on workers' rights.

weekly.title: German state elections deal a blow to Chancellor Friedrich Merz
weekly.summary: Elections in Berlin and Mecklenburg-Western Pomerania have dealt the CDU a historic defeat while the AfD saw a massive gain. The pressure on Germany's unpopular chancellor is mounting.

weekly.title: AfD makes gains in state elections but has no government options
weekly.summary: Despite making significant gains in both Berlin and Mecklenburg-Western Pomerania, the far-right AfD remains without options to form a state government.

weekly.title: Germany faces energy tax losses as EV sales rise
weekly.summary: The rapid shift to electric vehicles in Germany is cutting fuel tax revenue for the government. As EV sales surge, policymakers face growing pressure to find new ways to fund roads and transportation infrastructure.

weekly.title: In cosmopolitan Berlin, elections still closed to foreigners
weekly.summary: A quarter of Berlin residents will have no say in the German capital's city-state election because they lack citizenship. That's the highest proportion of residents excluded from the election yet, and many are unhappy.

weekly.title: Germany news: Doctors offer Oktoberfest flu jabs
weekly.summary: Oktoberfest 2026 is underway but it's not just beer on offer in Munich this year; revelers can also get themselves a flu jab before heading to the tents. DW has more.

weekly.title: Germany: Is it possible to replace the chancellor?
weekly.summary: Chancellor Friedrich Merz's record-low approval ratings have emboldened his opponents. There are three ways to remove a chancellor from office in Germany.

weekly.title: Summer of 2026 broke records in Europe, and caused deaths
weekly.summary: The summer of 2026 was not only the hottest on record in Europe, it also saw a record number of people die. More than 16,000 are thought to have died because of the heat in Germany alone.

weekly.title: German-Russian relations at freezing point
weekly.summary: Russia's full-scale invasion of Ukraine destroyed the once-close relationship between Moscow and Berlin. Yet the far-right AfD is calling for a normalization of relations.

weekly.title: Ukraine steps up measures to protect railways
weekly.summary: As Russia increases its attacks on Ukraine's rail infrastructure, the Ukrainian government has called for help to replace destroyed locomotives and is making plans to keep passengers safe.

weekly.title: Mecklenburg-Western Pomerania: Will economy shape the vote?
weekly.summary: Voters in the eastern state of Mecklenburg-Western Pomerania head to the polls on Sunday, with the Social Democrats and far-right AfD neck and neck. Here's a look at key economic issues that could influence the election.

weekly.title: Oktoberfest 2026: Everything you need to know
weekly.summary: This year, AI will be used to manage overcrowded situations. Find all the numbers surrounding the fest — including the price of water!

weekly.title: Rebels, workers, radicals: The making of 'Red Berlin'
weekly.summary: Bloody May, student sit-ins and the squatter movement: Berlin has long been a hotbed for working-class organizing and radical left-wing politics.

weekly.title: Mecklenburg-Western Pomerania: SPD seeks to fend off AfD
weekly.summary: For nearly three decades, the Social Democrats have governed Germany's northeastern state. If they can fend off the AfD, the result may boost the fortunes of the German government's junior coalition partner.

weekly.title: Ever more Israelis moving to and investing in Cyprus
weekly.summary: Over the past three years, more and more Israelis have been purchasing property and investing in Cyprus, with many moving to the island permanently. How has this changed the Cypriot economy and how are locals responding?

weekly.title: Women's football in Germany booming, but still much to do
weekly.summary: Women's football is growing rapidly, particularly in Germany. Nevertheless, equal pay and investment remain major talking points.

weekly.title: Strait of Hormuz attacks spill oil into Persian Gulf
weekly.summary: As war disrupts one of the world's busiest shipping lanes, satellite images reveal that oil is spreading toward protected coral reefs and mangrove forests.

weekly.title: Airport malaria in Germany remains infrequent
weekly.summary: An outbreak of malaria at Frankfurt Airport this summer has raised alarm. Experts believe parasites probably arrived in a passenger's luggage. But with the onset of fall, the risks of contracting the disease are low.

weekly.title: Fact Check: False video alleges Berlin votes destroyed
weekly.summary: A video claiming to show AfD postal ballots being destroyed has gone viral ahead of Berlin's September 20 election. DW Fact Check examines the footage, the accounts sharing it and how widely it is really being viewed.

weekly.title: German police probe arson attack on Wuppertal synagogue
weekly.summary: The man detained shortly after allegedly trying to set fire to Wuppertal's synagogue made antisemitic comments to the arresting officers, prosecutors say. The 37-year-old Afghan citizen also had knives in his apartment.

weekly.title: Canada and EU: A look at the bloc's special relationships
weekly.summary: Though Canada may be some distance from Europe geographically, closer political ties are in the cards. With talk of an associate membership, DW takes a look at other arrangements the EU has with particular countries.

weekly.title: Dual citizenship means Germany now in competition for talent
weekly.summary: Coach Jürgen Klopp has named several players to his first Germany squad who are eligible to play for other countries. Some still aren't committed to playing for thje national team long-term.

weekly.title: Beethoven and Andy Warhol: Rebel icons on show in Bonn
weekly.summary: The new exhibition "Beethoven by Warhol" at the Beethoven House in Bonn presents the pop artist's late masterpiece: a picture of Ludwig van Beethoven. The exhibition shares the story of the work with the public.

weekly.title: 'No compromises': Far-right AfD has few potential partners
weekly.summary: Germany's far-right AfD party is riding high after its latest electoral triumph in Saxony-Anhalt. But one question remains: Does it actually want to govern?

weekly.title: VAR's mission creep a problem for football
weekly.summary: After a decade of use, questions around VAR in football are louder than ever. Has the technology strayed too far from its remit?

weekly.title: Organized crime and drug-related deaths rise Germany
weekly.summary: In the annual report on organized crime, German police say cocaine is a danger for the state and society and cases of money laundering have increased.

weekly.title: Russian birth tourism to Brazil increases
weekly.summary: Since Russia's full-scale invasion of Ukraine and stricter regulations in Argentina, more and more Russians are choosing to travel to Brazil to give birth to children, who will obtain Brazilian nationality.

weekly.title: A war-fatigued and anxious Russia picks a new parliament
weekly.summary: Fuel shortages, drone strikes and mobilization rumors are fueling anxiety and war fatigue in Russia. As support for peace talks grows among Russians, the Kremlin is watching closely ahead of parliamentary elections.

weekly.title: Alexander Ovechkin backs Putin party in campaign video
weekly.summary: Ice hockey legend Alexander Ovechkin has lent Vladimir Putin's party a helping hand in its parliamentary election campaign. That's in keeping with a pattern of support by an athlete who claims not to be political.

weekly.title: Klopp wants Germany's football team to 'reclaim the flag'
weekly.summary: Jürgen Klopp, Germany's new head coach, says he wants his team to reclaim pride in being German after recent political developments.

weekly.title: Serbian President Vucic criticizes Kosovo war crimes verdict
weekly.summary: The conviction of four former Kosovo Liberation Army leaders has drawn sharply different reactions across the Balkans. Serbia has accused the court of failing to fully address crimes against Serbs.

weekly.title: King Charles, Earl Spencer clash over Diana death once again
weekly.summary: Buckingham Palace has rejected criticism of King Charles III in a new book by the brother of his late wife, Princess Diana. Earl Charles Spencer has been a fierce critic of his former brother-in-law for decades.

weekly.title: Jews once lived lived here: When houses tell stories
weekly.summary: Time and again, residents tracing the history of their homes discover the lives of Jewish predecessors who fled or were deported amid stories of suffering and loss.

weekly.title: Jürgen Klopp's first Germany squad includes 44 players
weekly.summary: Germany's new head coach Jürgen Klopp has named a huge squad for his first four games, splitting them into two groups. A host of new faces is included.

weekly.title: Saint, sinner or feminist icon: How Mary Magdalene's image evolved through time
weekly.summary: From "Apostle of the Apostles" to prostitute, Mary Magdalene has been assigned a wide variety of roles, as a new exhibition shows.

developing.title: India news: PM Modi says developing nations unfairly blamed for emissions
developing.summary: PM Narendra Modi has told a climate conference that developed countries emit six times more CO2 than India. Meanwhile, an IIT Bombay professor has been accused of caste abuse. DW has more.

developing.title: Live updates: Trump welcomes Xi to Washington
developing.summary: Donald Trump welcomes Xi Jinping to the US by greeting him personally at the tarmac at Joint Base Andrews. The two are expected to discuss trade, AI, Taiwan and Iran.
